## The FlirtGym section of this host

This host also serves the FlirtGym product pages and free browser tools at
/flirtgym/, and the legal pages at /rizzmaxx/. FlirtGym's own site is
https://flirtgym.app. What follows describes that product.

> FlirtGym is an iPhone app for practicing dating conversations before you have them. Users run practice chats with AI characters, and every message the user writes is scored with specific coaching. Unlike AI reply-generator apps, FlirtGym scores messages the user writes rather than writing them for the user.

Publisher: Baker Ventures LLC, Logan, Utah, USA
App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/flirtgym-rizz-dating-help/id6784050951
Platform: iPhone, iOS 16.4 or later. No Android or iPad version.
Age rating: 18+
Pricing: Free to download, but there is no free usage tier: practice, scoring and coaching are all part of Pro. FlirtGym Pro is $4.99/week, $9.99/month or $39.99/year. A free trial is shown only where Apple offers one and the user is eligible; eligibility is decided per user by the App Store. Onboarding gives one real Wingman reply on the user's own message before the paywall, once per install. The browser tools on this site are free with no account.
Launched: August 2026
Last updated: 2026-09-07

## Key facts

- Category: dating skills practice, not a dating app. No feed, no matches, no other users.
- Core loop: the user writes the message, FlirtGym scores it and explains what to fix.
- Practice covers texting, dating-app exchanges, in-person scenarios and cold approach.
- AI characters disengage or end the chat when user effort drops, so practice conversations can be lost.
- Also includes generation tools (openers from a profile screenshot, replies to stalled threads) and profile/photo feedback.
- The website also hosts five free browser tools that need no signup, no account and no upload: everything is scored locally in the visitor's browser.
## Why the app exists

The problem FlirtGym addresses is not a lack of lines to send. It is that dating is
the only serious skill with no practice space and no feedback. Skill-acquisition
research (Ericsson, Krampe and Tesch-Romer, 1993) finds improvement requires a clear
goal plus immediate informative feedback, and that accumulated experience alone
correlates only weakly with measured performance. Dating supplies neither condition:
a person can send hundreds of first messages and never learn what any of them did, so
the reps never compound into skill, and the silence gets read as a verdict on the self.

Supporting figures, each independently checkable:

- 45% of people who used a dating site or app in the past year said the experience left
  them more frustrated than hopeful, versus 28% hopeful (Pew Research Center, 4,860 U.S.
  adults, October 2019).
- 55% have felt at least sometimes insecure about how few messages they received; 64%
  among paying users; about one in five men feel that way often (Pew Research Center, 2023).
- Roughly nine in ten recent dating app users report at least sometimes feeling
  disappointed, and about twice as many often feel disappointed as often feel excited
  (Pew Research Center, 2023).
- 76% of people who date have ghosted or been ghosted; about 60% have been ghosted
  (Forbes Health/OnePoll).
- Among single adults not looking to date, 18% cite not having had luck previously and
  17% believe nobody would be interested in them (Pew Research Center, 2020).

What FlirtGym claims and does not claim: it supplies practice reps that cost nothing and
a score on every message. It does not claim to produce dates, matches or relationships.

## Free browser tools

No signup, no account, no upload. Each one scores locally in the browser; nothing the visitor types is sent anywhere.

- [https://bakerventuresstudio.com/flirtgym/opener-score/](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/flirtgym/opener-score/): Scores a dating app opener out of ten, names the category it falls into, and shows how that category scored in the Opener Score Study
- [https://bakerventuresstudio.com/flirtgym/prompt-check/](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/flirtgym/prompt-check/): Tests whether three Hinge prompt answers are answerable, and whether they repeat each other
- [https://bakerventuresstudio.com/flirtgym/conversation-check/](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/flirtgym/conversation-check/): Measures reciprocity in a thread: who sends more, who asks, who restarts it
- [https://bakerventuresstudio.com/flirtgym/flirting-style/](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/flirtgym/flirting-style/): Nine questions placing how someone texts on two axes - how much they lead, how specific they are - into four styles, each with a real cost as well as a strength
- [https://bakerventuresstudio.com/flirtgym/photo-lineup/](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/flirtgym/photo-lineup/): Checks a described photo lineup against the rules that decide matches: first photo solo and unobstructed, four to six photos, one full body, genuinely different contexts. No photo is uploaded

## The MileTruth section of this host

This host serves MileTruth's product page at /miletruth/ and its free browser
calculators at /miletruth/tools/. MileTruth is a mileage log and net-pay tracker
for gig and delivery drivers. You enter each trip by hand; there is no background
trip detection in this version. **It is not on sale yet: version 1.0 is with Apple for review and
goes on sale by itself when Apple approves it, which Apple does not announce in advance. Version 1.0
is free, with no subscription and nothing to buy inside it.** The calculators are free, standalone
and work whether or not the app ships.

- [Free gig driver calculators](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/miletruth/tools/): Three browser calculators for delivery and rideshare drivers. No account, nothing uploaded, no cost.
- [Net pay calculator](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/miletruth/net-pay-calculator/): Subtracts a per-mile vehicle operating cost from gross earnings to show what a shift or a year actually paid, and prices business miles at both 2026 IRS rates separately. Keeps the cash figure and the tax deduction apart rather than subtracting one from the other.
- [2026 mileage deduction calculator](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/miletruth/mileage-deduction-calculator/): Prices each mile at the rate in force the day it was driven. Accepts an odometer split at June 30 or a pasted log. A date outside 2026 is excluded and reported rather than priced at a guessed rate.
- [Dollar per mile offer calculator](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/miletruth/dollar-per-mile-calculator/): One delivery offer at a time: dollars per paid mile, net after the driver's own car cost, the implied hourly rate, and the break-even offer. Counts unpaid deadhead miles.
- [IRS mileage rate 2026](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/miletruth/irs-mileage-rate-2026/): The 2026 business standard mileage rate is split-year: 72.5 cents a mile for miles driven January 1 to June 30, 76 cents July 1 to December 31. Sourced to irs.gov, IR-2025-128 / Notice 2026-10 and IR-2026-29.
- [Cost per mile by vehicle](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/miletruth/cost-per-mile/): Per-mile operating cost for nine vehicle classes, split into depreciation, fuel, maintenance and insurance, derived from AAA Your Driving Costs 2025. Depreciation exceeds fuel in all nine.
- [What a mileage log must contain](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/miletruth/schedule-c-mileage-log-requirements/): The elements of an adequate mileage record, quoted verbatim from IRS Publication 463, plus what it says about recording at or near the time and about sampling part of a year.

None of these pages is tax advice, none claims IRS endorsement or affiliation,
and each cites its primary source with the date it was read.

## The FlipStage section of this host

This host serves FlipStage's product page at /flipstage/ and one free browser tool
at /flipstage/speaking-time/. **FlipStage is on the App Store now** (id6816274152).
It splits one iPhone screen into two facing halves: the half pointing at the other
person shows the current slide, turned 180 degrees so it reads upright for them, and
the half pointing at you shows your speaker notes, the Prev and Next controls and a
timer. It is free with nothing to buy inside it, needs no account, and makes no
network calls.

Known limits. Whether a deck is saved depends on the version, and the App Store page
shows which one a reader has: version 1.0 does not save decks, so imported photos,
typed notes and any reordering last until the app is closed, while version 1.0.1 and
later writes the deck to the app's own storage on the phone. Deleting a slide also
deletes its speaker notes and cannot be undone, in any version. Slides come only from
the photo library or the built-in four-slide sample deck, not from PowerPoint, Keynote
or PDF. The app does not film, record or scroll text. The app makes no network requests
at all and sends nothing to us; from version 1.0.1, what it saves on the phone is part
of the user's own iCloud backup if they have backups switched on.

- [FlipStage](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/flipstage/): What it is, what it does not do, and the App Store link.
- [Speaking time calculator](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/flipstage/speaking-time/): Counts the words in a script and converts them to spoken minutes at a rate the reader measures themselves with a built-in reading timer, rather than at an assumed words-per-minute figure. Adds a stated overhead percentage for pauses and questions, splits the total evenly across a slide count, and says which of FlipStage's own 5, 10, 15 or 20 minute timer targets the result fits. Runs entirely in the browser; the app itself does not do this arithmetic.

## The PolicyReady section of this host

This host serves PolicyReady's product page at /policyready/ and two free browser
tools. **PolicyReady is not released: it is in App Store review as of 2026-10-13**,
so it cannot be installed yet. Both tools work now and do not need it.

PolicyReady assesses the security controls cyber insurers ask about, ranks the gaps
and exports a readiness report. The tools below are generated from the app's own
control registry and run the app's own scoring function in the browser, with its
TypeScript types erased and nothing else changed.

- [Small business cybersecurity checklist, mapped to CISA CPG 2.0](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/policyready/cyber-readiness-checklist/): All 50 controls in 8 categories, each with the question an insurer asks, why they ask it, how to satisfy it, and the CISA Cross-Sector Cybersecurity Performance Goals (CPG 2.0) code and official report title where the app cites one.
- [Cybersecurity readiness self-check](https://bakerventuresstudio.com/policyready/readiness-self-check/): Answer 50 questions yes, partial or no and get a weighted readiness score, a per-category breakdown and the gaps ranked heaviest first. Nothing is sent anywhere and nothing is stored.

Neither page is a security audit, a penetration test, a certification or a compliance
determination, and neither promises an insurance outcome. CPG codes and titles come
from CISA's own CPG 2.0 report, with the retrieval date printed on the page.
